name: MN-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
Long-serving incumbent Betty McCollum running for re-election
Massive fundraising gap: McCollum has raised over $1.25 million to under $30,000 for Paul Wikstrom
Prediction markets price McCollum at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: This suburban Twin Cities seat leans Democratic by 18 points, McCollum is a well-established incumbent, and she holds an overwhelming financial advantage with no outside spending against her. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based expectation.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or an unexpectedly strong national Republican wave environment would be the main things that could narrow this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Betty McCollum, a Democratic incumbent first elected in 2000, is seeking re-election in a St. Paul-area district that leans Democratic by 18 points. She has raised about $1.25 million and holds nearly $500,000 in cash, while Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised under $30,000 with almost nothing banked. No outside groups are spending against her, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give McCollum roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and there are no public general-election polls to suggest otherwise. With the incumbent renominated and the fundamentals strongly favoring her party, this seat is rated Safe Democratic, with McCollum expected to win by a margin in the low-to-mid twenty-point range.
